form_analysis.feedback: Highly specialised aftercare form for compromised skin. Excellently frames aftercare as a direct continuation of the treatment's reparative goal. Provides clear, non-negotiable rules about avoiding all irritants and supporting the lipid barrier. Strong patient education component.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is a critical extension of your treatment. Your skin barrier has been supported with reparative ingredients; the goal now is to protect this fragile new foundation and allow it to strengthen without disruption.

instructions.general_directive: Follow this 'skin holiday' protocol strictly. The key principle is to DO LESS. Allow your skin to heal itself with minimal intervention.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: Your skin should feel immediately soothed, less tight, and more comfortable. Any pre-existing redness may be slightly pinker for 12-24 hours before improving. As your barrier recovers over 3-7 days, you will notice increased resilience, less reactivity, and better hydration retention.

sections.title: The Repair Phase: Product Protocol
items: For the next 7-14 days, use ONLY the ultra-gentle, barrier-repair products recommended by your therapist (typically containing ceramides, cholesterol, fatty acids, and soothing agents like panthenol).
STOP ALL ACTIVE INGREDIENTS: Absolutely no retinoids/retinol, AHAs/BHAs, Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid), benzoyl peroxide, or physical scrubs. These will break down your new lipid barrier.
Cleanse only once per day (in the evening) with a milky or cream cleanser, using lukewarm water. In the morning, just splash with water.
Apply your reparative moisturizer to slightly damp skin to lock in water.

sections.title: Avoiding Barrier Disruption
sections.content: Do not use washcloths, cleansing brushes, muslin cloths, or any abrasive tools. Use only your clean fingertips. Avoid tap water with high mineral content (hard water) if possible; micellar water can be a gentle alternative for cleansing.

sections.title: Sun and Environmental Protection
items: A compromised barrier is vulnerable to UV and pollution. Use a gentle mineral sunscreen (zinc oxide is ideal) every morning.
Avoid extreme weather, windy conditions, and heavily air-conditioned or heated environments.

sections.title: Activity and Lifestyle
items: Avoid anything that causes significant facial flushing or sweating: intense exercise, hot yoga, saunas, spicy food, and alcohol for at least 72 hours.
Manage stress and ensure adequate sleep, as these directly impact barrier function.
Consider changing pillowcases frequently to a soft, natural fabric like silk or satin.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: It is strongly advised to avoid all makeup for a minimum of 48 hours, and ideally for 3-5 days to let the barrier seal. When resuming, choose minimal, non-comedogenic products.

sections.title: Signs of Healing
sections.content: Positive signs that your barrier is repairing include: reduced sensitivity, less stinging when applying products, diminished redness, improved hydration (skin feels supple, not tight), and fewer random breakouts or dry patches.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: If you experience a temporary increase in small, flesh-colored bumps (closed comedones), it may be your skin adjusting to richer creams. This often settles. Contact your therapist if it persists.
True barrier repair is a slow process. Initial calming is immediate, but a stronger, more resilient barrier is built over 2-4 weeks of consistent, gentle care.
Contact your therapist if you experience any severe itching, burning, or a rash.
